riskDescription: Risk that required documents are not obtained from the customer as per the defined checklist before creating a new customer code in the customer master, leading to incomplete or unauthorized customer records.
controlObjective: To ensure that all required documents are obtained from the customer as per the defined checklist before customer master creation.
controlActivity: The AM – Bid & Auctions (WHO) checks (WHAT) the documents received from the customer (WHERE - physical documents) at the time of receipt (WHEN) against the defined checklist (IPE-1) approved by SM – Strategy & Management (HOW), to ensure all necessary information is available for customer master creation (WHY).
controlEvidence: Signed checklist (IPE-1), customer documents.
sopSectionReference: Page 12, Process Narrative CM-C1, Control C1
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not specify how the AM – Bid & Auctions verifies the authenticity of the documents beyond self-attestation. 2. No mention of a secondary review of the checklist completion by a supervisor.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain a sample of customer master creation requests. 2. Obtain the corresponding customer documents and signed checklist (IPE-1). 3. Obtain the approved checklist (IPE-1) from SM – Strategy & Management.
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that the AM – Bid & Auctions checked the documents against the checklist (IPE-1). 2. Verify that all required documents as per IPE-1 were received.

riskDescription: Risk that customer’s self-attested documents are not obtained or are not genuinely self-attested, leading to unverified or fraudulent customer records.
controlObjective: To ensure the authenticity and proper attestation of all customer documents received for customer master creation.
controlActivity: The AM – Bid & Auctions (WHO) checks (WHAT) that all documents received from the customer (WHERE - physical documents) are self-attested by the customer in ink (HOW) at the time of receipt (WHEN), to prevent the use of scanned or photocopied documents and ensure authenticity (WHY).
controlEvidence: Self-attested customer documents, signed checklist (IPE-1).
sopSectionReference: Page 12, Process Narrative CM-C1, Control C2
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not specify a process for verifying the signature on the self-attested documents. 2. No mention of a periodic review of customer master data for potential fraudulent entries.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain a sample of customer master creation requests. 2. Obtain the corresponding self-attested customer documents. 3. Obtain the signed checklist (IPE-1).
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that all documents are self-attested in ink. 2. Verify that no scanned/photocopied documents were accepted.

riskDescription: Risk that required documents are not obtained from the customer before creating a new customer code in the customer master, leading to incomplete or unauthorized customer records.
controlObjective: To ensure that all required documents are formally acknowledged as received and complete by the responsible personnel.
controlActivity: The AM – Bid & Auctions (WHO) fills and signs off (WHAT) the pre-defined checklist (IPE-1) (WHERE - physical document) post receipt of all required documents (WHEN), to formally validate that all necessary documents have been received from the customer (WHY).
controlEvidence: Signed checklist (IPE-1).
sopSectionReference: Page 13, Process Narrative CM-C5, Control C3
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not specify a review of the signed checklist by a higher authority to ensure the AM – Bid & Auctions has performed the check diligently. 2. No mention of archiving the signed checklist for audit trail purposes.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain a sample of customer master creation requests. 2. Obtain the corresponding signed checklist (IPE-1).
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that the checklist (IPE-1) is completely filled and signed off by the AM – Bid & Auctions. 2. Verify the date of sign-off aligns with the receipt of documents.

riskDescription: Risk that incorrect information, including credit terms, is filled in the Customer Master Creation Form (IPE-2), leading to inaccurate customer master data and potential financial misstatements.

controlActivity: The TPA IT Executive (WHO) verifies (WHAT) the details in the Customer Master Creation Form (IPE-2) (WHERE - physical document) against the supporting documents (IPE-1) and the Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) (HOW) upon receipt of the form (WHEN), to ensure accuracy and completeness of the information before customer code creation (WHY).
controlEvidence: Customer Master Creation Form (IPE-2), supporting documents (IPE-1), PPA.

sopSectionReference: Page 14, Process Narrative CM-C6, Control C4
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not specify a formal sign-off or evidence of this verification by the TPA IT Executive on the IPE-2 form itself. 2. No mention of a defined checklist or procedure for the TPA IT Executive's verification process.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain a sample of Customer Master Creation Forms (IPE-2). 2. Obtain corresponding supporting documents (IPE-1) and PPA. 3. Obtain evidence of TPA IT Executive's verification (e.g., email confirmation, sign-off).
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that the details in IPE-2, especially credit terms, match IPE-1 and PPA. 2. Verify that the TPA IT Executive performed the verification before customer code creation.

riskDescription: Risk of delay in sending the Customer Master Creation Form (IPE-2) along with supporting documents to the TPA IT Executive, resulting in delay in customer code creation in ERP and potential operational inefficiencies.
controlObjective: To ensure timely submission of complete customer master creation documentation to the TPA IT Executive for efficient customer code creation.
controlActivity: The AM – Bid & Auctions (WHO) sends (WHAT) the Customer Master Creation Form (IPE-2) along with the signed checklist (IPE-1) and supporting documents (WHERE - via email/shared drive) to the TPA IT Executive (HOW) within 1 day of filling the form (WHEN), to prevent delays in customer code creation in ERP (WHY).
controlEvidence: Email logs, shared drive timestamps, dispatch records.
sopSectionReference: Page 15, Process Narrative CM-C7, Control C5
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not specify a mechanism for the TPA IT Executive to acknowledge receipt and timestamp the documents, making it difficult to track adherence to the 1-day timeline. 2. No escalation matrix defined for delays beyond the 1-day timeline.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain a sample of Customer Master Creation Forms (IPE-2) and associated communication records (e.g., emails) from AM – Bid & Auctions. 2. Obtain corresponding receipt acknowledgements from TPA IT Executive.
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that the form and documents were sent to the TPA IT Executive within 1 day of the AM – Bid & Auctions filling the form.

riskDescription: Risk that missing documents or information are not identified and communicated back to the AM – Bid & Auctions, leading to incomplete customer master data creation.

controlActivity: The TPA IT Executive (WHO) checks (WHAT) the completeness of the documents/information received against the defined checklist (IPE-1) (HOW) within 1 day of receipt of the form (IPE-2) from AM – Bid & Auctions (WHEN), and in case of missing items, provides a Gap report (IPE-3) along with a listing of missing information to AM – Bid & Auctions (WHERE - via email/system) (WHY - to facilitate complete customer master creation).
controlEvidence: Gap report (IPE-3), email communication.
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not specify a formal template or mandatory fields for the Gap report (IPE-3). 2. No defined escalation path if the AM – Bid & Auctions fails to provide missing documents after the Gap report.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain a sample of customer master creation requests where a Gap report (IPE-3) was issued. 2. Obtain the corresponding Gap report (IPE-3) and communication records.
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that the TPA IT Executive issued a Gap report for missing documents/information. 2. Verify the timeliness of the Gap report issuance.

riskDescription: Risk of delay by AM – Bid & Auctions in providing missing information/documents as per the Gap report (IPE-3), leading to further delays in customer code creation.
controlObjective: To ensure timely submission of missing documents/information by AM – Bid & Auctions to the TPA IT Executive after receiving a Gap report.
controlActivity: The AM – Bid & Auctions (WHO) provides (WHAT) all the required information/documents as per the Gap report (IPE-3) (WHERE - via email/shared drive) to the TPA IT Executive (HOW) within 2 days of receipt of the Gap report (WHEN), to avoid further delays in customer master creation (WHY).
controlEvidence: Email logs, shared drive timestamps, Gap report (IPE-3).
sopSectionReference: Page 17, Process Narrative CM-C11, Control C6
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not specify a mechanism for the TPA IT Executive to track the 2-day timeline and escalate non-compliance. 2. No defined consequences for repeated delays by AM – Bid & Auctions.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain a sample of Gap reports (IPE-3) issued by TPA IT Executive. 2. Obtain corresponding communication records from AM – Bid & Auctions providing the missing documents.
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that AM – Bid & Auctions provided the missing documents within 2 days of receiving the Gap report.

riskDescription: Risk that incomplete customer details are entered in the Customer Master (IPE-4) in ERP, leading to inaccurate customer records and potential financial misstatements.
controlObjective: To ensure that all critical customer details are mandatorily captured in the ERP system during customer master creation.
controlActivity: The ERP system (WHERE) is configured (HOW) to define specific fields (Customer Name, Customer Address, PAN, Receivable terms, Bank Account Number, Bank Name, and IFSC Code) as mandatory (WHAT) at the time of customer master creation (WHEN), to prevent the creation of incomplete customer records (WHY).
controlEvidence: ERP system configuration screenshots, user access matrix, system audit logs.
sopSectionReference: Page 18, Process Narrative CM-C12, Control C7
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not specify a periodic review process for mandatory fields configuration in ERP to ensure continued relevance and effectiveness. 2. No mention of a change management process for mandatory field definitions.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain ERP system configuration settings for customer master creation. 2. Obtain a sample of newly created customer master records (IPE-4).
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that the specified fields (Customer Name, Address, PAN, Receivable terms, Bank Account Number, Bank Name, IFSC Code) are configured as mandatory in ERP. 2. Attempt to create a customer master record with one of these fields left blank to confirm system enforcement.

riskDescription: Risk that unauthorized customer codes are created in the customer master (IPE-4) in ERP, potentially leading to fraudulent transactions or misstatements.

controlActivity: The IT department (WHO) restricts (WHAT) access rights to create customer master (IPE-4) in the ERP system (WHERE) to only authorized personnel (HOW) on an ongoing basis (WHEN), to prevent unauthorized or fraudulent customer code creation (WHY).
controlEvidence: ERP user access matrix, access request forms, approval records, system logs.

sopSectionReference: Page 18, Process Narrative CM-C12, Control C8
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not specify a periodic review process for user access rights to customer master creation. 2. No mention of a process for revoking access upon role change or termination. 3. The SOP does not define who the "authorized personnel" are by role/designation.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain the ERP user access matrix for customer master creation. 2. Obtain a list of personnel authorized to create customer master records. 3. Obtain sample access request and approval forms.
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that only authorized personnel have access to create customer master records in ERP. 2. Verify that access rights are granted based on approved requests. 3. Verify that there is no conflict of interest for personnel with creation access.

riskDescription: Risk that the Accounts Receivable SOP, including customer master creation procedures, becomes outdated or inaccurate, leading to non-compliance with internal policies or regulatory requirements.

controlActivity: The Director - Finance (WHO) reviews and approves (WHAT) the Accounts Receivable SOP (WHERE - document management system) annually (WHEN) or upon significant process changes (HOW), to ensure its continued relevance, accuracy, and compliance with internal controls and regulatory requirements (WHY).
controlEvidence: Approved SOP versions, review meeting minutes, sign-off sheets.
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not explicitly state a policy for periodic review and update of the document itself. 2. No mention of version control mechanisms for the SOP.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain the latest version of the Accounts Receivable SOP. 2. Obtain previous versions and evidence of review/approval.
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that the SOP has been reviewed and approved by the Director - Finance at least annually. 2. Verify that version control is maintained.

riskDescription: Risk that customer master data becomes outdated, inaccurate, or contains redundant/inactive entries, leading to incorrect billing, misstatements in accounts receivable, or potential fraud.
controlObjective: To ensure the ongoing accuracy, completeness, and validity of customer master data in the ERP system.
controlActivity: The Manager - Accounts (WHO) reviews (WHAT) a report of active and inactive customer master records (WHERE - ERP system) on a quarterly basis (WHEN), comparing it against business activity and supporting documentation (HOW), to identify and initiate deactivation of redundant or inactive customer codes and correct any inaccuracies (WHY).
controlEvidence: Quarterly customer master review reports, evidence of deactivation requests, approval records.
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not explicitly mention a process for periodic review and cleanup of existing customer master data. 2. No defined criteria for identifying inactive or redundant customer codes.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain quarterly customer master review reports. 2. Obtain evidence of follow-up actions (e.g., deactivation requests, corrections).
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that the Manager - Accounts performs the review quarterly. 2. Verify that identified discrepancies or inactive codes are appropriately addressed.

riskDescription: Risk of duplicate customer codes being created in the ERP system, leading to inaccurate customer records, potential misapplication of payments, and reporting errors.
controlObjective: To ensure that unique customer master records are maintained in the ERP system and duplicate entries are prevented.
controlActivity: The ERP system (WHERE) automatically (HOW) restricts the creation of a new customer code (WHAT) if a duplicate PAN number is detected (WHEN), and provides a warning to the TPA IT Executive (WHO) to prevent the entry of redundant or erroneous customer records (WHY).
controlEvidence: ERP system logs, customer master data.
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP mentions a warning, but it's unclear if the TPA IT Executive is mandated to take specific action (e.g., investigate, reject) when a warning is triggered, or if the system allows override.2. The SOP does not specify the exact criteria for "duplicate details" beyond PAN.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain a sample of new customer code creation requests from the ERP system.2. Obtain ERP system configuration for duplicate check rules (e.g., PAN uniqueness).3. Obtain system logs for instances where duplicate warnings were triggered.
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that the ERP system prevents creation of customer codes with duplicate PANs.2. For instances where warnings were triggered, verify that the TPA IT Executive investigated and resolved the potential duplicate, or provided justification for proceeding.

riskDescription: Risk of incorrect PAN numbers being recorded in the customer master, leading to incorrect TDS deductions, potential non-compliance with tax regulations, and financial penalties.
controlObjective: To ensure the accuracy and validity of PAN details in the customer master for correct tax compliance.
controlActivity: The TPA IT Executive (WHO) cross-checks the PAN details (WHAT) through the internet (WHERE) at the time of customer master creation (WHEN) to ensure the correctness of the PAN (WHY) before updating it in the ERP system (HOW).
controlEvidence: Screenshot of PAN verification, customer master creation form (IPE-2).
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not specify which internet source (e.g., official income tax portal) should be used for verification.2. There is no explicit requirement for documenting the PAN verification (e.g., screenshot, verification log).3. No independent review of this cross-check is mentioned.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain a sample of new customer master creation requests.2. Obtain supporting documents including PAN details.3. Obtain evidence of PAN verification (if any is documented).
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that the PAN details in the customer master match the supporting documents.2. Independently verify the PAN details for the selected samples using an official online portal.

riskDescription: Risk of inaccurate customer details being entered into the customer master, leading to incorrect billing, communication issues, and financial reporting errors.

controlActivity: The TPA IT Manager (WHO) verifies the customer code details in the customer master (IPE-4) (WHERE) against the Customer Master Creation Form (IPE-2) and supporting documents (IPE-1) (HOW) within 1 day of creation of customer details (WHEN), to ensure the accuracy of the entered information (WHY).
controlEvidence: Customer Master Creation Form (IPE-2), supporting documents (IPE-1), ERP customer master record (IPE-4), verification sign-off.

gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not specify what action the TPA IT Manager should take if discrepancies are found during verification.2. No explicit documentation of the verification (e.g., checklist sign-off) is mentioned, only that the manager "verifies".
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain a sample of customer master creation requests and corresponding ERP entries (IPE-4).2. Obtain Customer Master Creation Forms (IPE-2) and supporting documents (IPE-1) for the selected samples.3. Obtain evidence of TPA IT Manager's verification (e.g., email approval, system workflow approval, sign-off).
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that the customer details in the ERP system (IPE-4) accurately match the Customer Master Creation Form (IPE-2) and supporting documents (IPE-1).2. Verify that the TPA IT Manager performed the verification within the stipulated timeline (within 1 day).

controlObjective: To ensure that access to the customer master is restricted to authorized personnel only, preventing unauthorized modifications or data breaches.
controlActivity: The ERP system (WHERE) strictly restricts access rights (WHAT) to the customer master (IPE-4) (HOW) to only authorized personnel (WHO) on an ongoing basis (WHEN), to prevent unauthorized access and data manipulation (WHY).
controlEvidence: Access matrix, user access logs, system configuration.

riskDescription: Risk that the customer code creation log is not maintained or reviewed, leading to undetected errors, unauthorized creations, or incomplete audit trails for customer master changes.

Verify that the log (IPE-5) is complete and accurately reflects new customer codes created in the ERP system.4. Verify that any discrepancies identified by the Internal Auditor were appropriately addressed.

riskDescription: Risk that the customer master is not reviewed on a timely basis, leading to outdated or inaccurate customer details, which can impact billing, communication, and financial reporting.
controlObjective: To ensure that the customer master is periodically reviewed for completeness and accuracy, and that this review process is adhered to.

The SOP does not define what constitutes "document (IPE-6)" or its required content.

Verify that SM – Strategy and Management checked the adherence of this activity on a half-yearly basis.3. Verify that the document (IPE-6) provides sufficient evidence of the review performed.

todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that AM – Bid & Auction checked all documents received against the defined checklist (IPE-1).2. Verify that all documents listed in the checklist were obtained and are relevant to the requested amendment.

remarks: Inferred from Process Narrative RT5 and Control Grid C35.

controlObjective: To ensure proper investigation and documentation of short receipts.
controlActivity: The TPA Executive (WHO) checks for short receipts of amount (WHAT) against the terms of the PPA (HOW) upon identifying a discrepancy (WHEN) to identify and document possible reasons such as cash discount, deductions, or outstanding balances (WHY).
controlEvidence: Short receipt records, PPA, Investigation notes
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not specify a formal documentation of the investigation findings. 2. No mention of a threshold for short receipts that triggers investigation.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain a sample of short receipt instances. 2. Obtain PPA terms. 3. Obtain TPA Executive's investigation records (if any).
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that short receipts are investigated against PPA terms. 2. Verify that reasons for short receipts are identified.
remediationActionPlan: Introduce a formal template for documenting short receipt investigations. Define a materiality threshold for triggering investigations.
remarks: Inferred from Process Narrative RT7 and Control Grid C36.

riskDescription: Risk that short receipts are not escalated or communicated to relevant stakeholders for resolution, leading to unresolved discrepancies.
controlObjective: To ensure timely escalation of short receipt discrepancies.
controlActivity: The TPA Executive (WHO) informs AM – Bid & Auctions and Manager - Accounts (WHAT) about any short receipt of amount along with possible reasons (IPE-12) (HOW) immediately upon identification (WHEN) to ensure timely escalation and resolution of discrepancies (WHY).
controlEvidence: Short receipt records, Communication records (IPE-12)
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not specify a formal record of this communication. 2. No defined escalation matrix or timeline for resolution.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain a sample of short receipt instances. 2. Obtain communication records (e.g., emails) to AM – Bid & Auctions and Manager - Accounts.
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that short receipts and their reasons are communicated to AM – Bid & Auctions and Manager - Accounts promptly.
remediationActionPlan: Introduce a formal communication log for short receipts. Define an escalation matrix and resolution timelines in the SOP.
remarks: Inferred from Process Narrative RT8 and Control Grid C37.

riskDescription: Risk that reasons for short receipts are not confirmed with customers, leading to unresolved discrepancies and potential write-offs.
controlObjective: To ensure customer confirmation of reasons for short receipts.
controlActivity: The AM – Bid & Auctions (WHO) follows up with the customer (WHAT) regarding short receipts (HOW) upon being informed by the TPA Executive (WHEN) to confirm the reasons for the discrepancy (IPE-12) (WHY).
controlEvidence: Customer communication records, Customer confirmation (IPE-12)
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not specify a formal record of customer follow-up and confirmation. 2. No defined timeline for customer follow-up.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain a sample of short receipt instances with customer communication. 2. Obtain records of customer follow-up (e.g., emails, call logs). 3. Obtain customer confirmation (IPE-12).
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that AM – Bid & Auctions follows up with customers for short receipts. 2. Verify that reasons for short receipts are confirmed by the customer.
remediationActionPlan: Introduce a formal log for customer follow-up and confirmation. Define a timeline for customer follow-up in the SOP.
remarks: Inferred from Process Narrative RT9 and Control Grid C38.

riskDescription: Risk that confirmed reasons for short receipts are not communicated back to the TPA Executive for proper accounting, leading to incorrect adjustments.
controlObjective: To ensure confirmed reasons for short receipts are communicated for accurate accounting.
controlActivity: The AM – Bid & Auctions (WHO) informs the TPA Executive through Manager – Accounts (WHAT) about the confirmed reasons (IPE-12) for short receipts (HOW) after customer confirmation (WHEN) to ensure accurate accounting adjustments can be made (WHY).
controlEvidence: Customer confirmation (IPE-12), Internal communication records
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not specify a formal record of this communication. 2. No defined timeline for communicating confirmed reasons.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain a sample of short receipt instances with customer confirmation. 2. Obtain communication records (e.g., emails) from AM – Bid & Auctions to TPA Executive via Manager – Accounts.
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that confirmed reasons for short receipts are communicated to the TPA Executive via Manager – Accounts.
remediationActionPlan: Introduce a formal communication log for confirmed short receipt reasons. Define a timeline for communication in the SOP.
remarks: Inferred from Process Narrative RT12 and Control Grid C39.

riskDescription: Risk that late receipts are not identified, leading to unbilled interest or uncollected revenue.
controlObjective: To ensure timely identification of late receipts for potential interest charges.
controlActivity: The TPA Executive (WHO) checks for late receipts (WHAT) by comparing actual receipt dates with due dates (HOW) on a daily basis (WHEN) to identify instances where interest may be chargeable (WHY).
controlEvidence: Bank statements, Customer invoices
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not specify a formal record of this daily check. 2. No clear definition of "late receipt" or threshold for triggering interest calculation.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain daily bank statements. 2. Obtain customer invoices with due dates. 3. Obtain TPA Executive's daily check records (if any).
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that the TPA Executive performs daily checks for late receipts. 2. For a sample of late receipts, verify that they were identified.
remediationActionPlan: Introduce a formal log for daily late receipt checks. Define "late receipt" and interest calculation thresholds in the SOP.
remarks: Inferred from Process Narrative RT13 and Control Grid C40.

riskDescription: Risk that interest for late receipts is not accurately calculated or recorded, leading to understatement of interest income.
controlObjective: To ensure accurate calculation and recording of interest on late receipts.
controlActivity: The TPA Manager (WHO) reviews the entries recorded in ERP (IPE-10) for interest on late receipts (WHAT) by verifying the calculation and GL coding (HOW) on a per transaction basis (WHEN) to ensure accurate and complete recording of interest income (WHY).
controlEvidence: ERP accounting entries (IPE-10), Interest calculation records
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not specify a formal sign-off or evidence of this review. 2. No mention of a system-based calculation for interest on late receipts.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain a sample of ERP entries for interest on late receipts. 2. Obtain supporting calculations for interest. 3. Obtain relevant policy for interest calculation.
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that the interest calculation is accurate as per policy. 2. Verify that the GL coding and amount recorded in ERP are correct.
remediationActionPlan: Introduce a formal sign-off by the TPA Manager on the reviewed interest entries. Explore system-based calculation for interest on late receipts.
remarks: Inferred from Process Narrative RT14 and Control Grid C41.

riskDescription: Risk that unauthorized debit notes for interest are raised, leading to incorrect customer charges or disputes.
controlObjective: To ensure all debit notes for interest are properly authorized.
controlActivity: The TPA Executive (WHO) obtains approval for raising debit notes (IPE-13) for interest (WHAT) as per the Delegation of Authority (DOA) matrix (HOW) before sharing with Manager - Accounts (WHEN) to ensure all debit notes are properly authorized (WHY).
controlEvidence: Debit note (IPE-13), Approval records, DOA matrix
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not explicitly state the DOA matrix for debit note approval. 2. No mention of a system workflow for approval.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain a sample of debit notes (IPE-13) for interest. 2. Obtain approval records (e.g., email, signed document). 3. Obtain the Delegation of Authority (DOA) matrix.
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that approval for raising debit notes was obtained from the authorized person as per the DOA matrix.
remediationActionPlan: Explicitly include the DOA matrix for debit note approval in the SOP. Explore implementing a system-based workflow for debit note approval.
remarks: Inferred from Process Narrative RT15 and Control Grid C42.

riskDescription: Risk that debit notes are raised incorrectly or without customer awareness, leading to customer disputes or uncollectible amounts.
controlObjective: To ensure accurate debit notes are raised and confirmed by the customer.
controlActivity: The AM – Bid & Auctions (WHO) checks and raises debit notes (IPE-13) on the customer (WHAT) for interest (HOW) and obtains confirmation from the customer via email (WHERE/HOW) upon approval (WHEN) to ensure accuracy and customer acceptance of the debit note (WHY).
controlEvidence: Debit note (IPE-13), Customer email confirmation
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not specify the detailed checks AM – Bid & Auctions performs before raising the debit note. 2. No defined timeline for obtaining customer confirmation.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain a sample of debit notes (IPE-13) raised. 2. Obtain customer confirmation via email. 3. Obtain supporting interest calculation.
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that the debit note details are accurate. 2. Verify that customer confirmation for the debit note was obtained.
remediationActionPlan: Define detailed checks for AM – Bid & Auctions before raising debit notes. Establish a clear timeline for obtaining customer confirmation.
remarks: Inferred from Process Narrative RT16 and Control Grid C43.

riskDescription: Risk that supporting documents for debit notes are not provided to the TPA Executive for recording, leading to unsupported accounting entries.
controlObjective: To ensure complete documentation for debit notes is provided for recording.
controlActivity: The Manager - Accounts (WHO) shares the scanned copy of the debit note (IPE-13) and customer confirmation (WHAT) with the TPA Executive (WHERE) promptly after receipt (WHEN) to ensure complete documentation is available for recording (WHY).
controlEvidence: Debit note (IPE-13), Customer confirmation, Communication records
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not specify a formal record of this sharing. 2. No defined timeline for "promptly after receipt."
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain a sample of debit notes (IPE-13) and customer confirmations. 2. Obtain records of sharing with TPA Executive (e.g., email).
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that the debit note and customer confirmation are shared with the TPA Executive. 2. Verify the timeliness of sharing.
remediationActionPlan: Introduce a formal log for sharing documents with the TPA Executive. Define a clear timeline for sharing documents.
remarks: Inferred from Process Narrative RT17 and Control Grid C44.

riskDescription: Risk of outdated or ineffective procedures due to lack of periodic review and update of the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP).
controlObjective: To ensure the Accounts Receivable SOP is current and effective.
controlActivity: The Director - Finance Control (WHO) reviews and updates the Accounts Receivable SOP (WHAT) annually (WHEN) to ensure it remains current, effective, and compliant with business operations and regulatory requirements (WHY) by incorporating process changes and feedback (HOW).
controlEvidence: SOP document control log, Approved SOP versions
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not explicitly state a review frequency or owner for the SOP itself.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain the latest version of the Accounts Receivable SOP. 2. Obtain previous versions of the SOP. 3. Obtain evidence of annual review and approval (e.g., sign-off sheet, document control log).
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that the Accounts Receivable SOP has been reviewed and approved annually by the Director - Finance Control. 2. Compare current and previous versions to identify updates.
remediationActionPlan: Establish a formal SOP review and update process with defined responsibilities and frequency.
remarks: Recommended governance control for SOP maintenance.

riskDescription: Risk of unauthorized access to ERP system functions due to dormant accounts, inappropriate access levels, or lack of timely revocation.
controlObjective: To ensure appropriate and authorized user access to ERP Accounts Receivable functions.
controlActivity: The IT Executive (WHO) performs a quarterly review of user access rights (WHAT) to the ERP system (WHERE) for Accounts Receivable functions (HOW) to ensure that access is appropriate, necessary, and promptly revoked for terminated employees or changed roles (WHY).
controlEvidence: User access review reports, ERP user access matrix, HR records
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not explicitly mention a periodic review of ERP access rights.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain quarterly user access review reports. 2. Obtain the user access matrix for ERP. 3. Obtain HR records for new hires, terminations, and role changes.
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that quarterly user access reviews are performed and documented. 2. For a sample of users, verify that their access rights are appropriate to their current roles. 3. Verify that access for terminated employees is promptly revoked.
remediationActionPlan: Implement a formal quarterly user access review process for ERP Accounts Receivable functions.
remarks: Recommended IT General Control for access management.

riskDescription: Risk of inaccurate, incomplete, or redundant customer master data due to lack of periodic data cleansing, leading to operational inefficiencies and financial errors.
controlObjective: To maintain the accuracy and integrity of customer master data.
controlActivity: The Manager - Accounts (WHO) performs a semi-annual review and cleansing of customer master data (WHAT) in the ERP system (WHERE) by identifying and correcting inaccuracies, completing missing information, and deactivating redundant or inactive customer codes (HOW) to maintain data integrity and accuracy (WHY).
controlEvidence: Customer master data review reports, ERP change logs
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not explicitly mention a periodic review or cleansing of customer master data.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain semi-annual customer master data review reports. 2. Obtain ERP system logs for customer master changes. 3. Obtain a sample of customer master records.
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that semi-annual customer master data reviews are performed and documented. 2. For a sample of identified inaccuracies or redundant codes, verify that corrective actions (e.g., updates, deactivations) were taken.
remediationActionPlan: Implement a formal semi-annual customer master data review and cleansing process.
remarks: Recommended control for master data governance.

subProcess: Customer Billing, Collection through RTGS, Collection through Cheque/Demand Draft
riskDescription: Risk that receivables are not recorded in the correct accounting period, leading to misstatement of financial results.
controlObjective: To ensure that all receivables are recorded in the correct accounting period.
controlActivity: The TPA Manager (WHO) checks (WHAT) that receivables are recorded in the correct period (WHY) by reviewing the available supporting documents (IPE-11) (HOW) in the ERP system (WHERE) on a monthly basis (WHEN).
controlEvidence: ERP system reports, IPE-11 documents, TPA Manager's review sign-off/report
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not define the specific reports or reconciliation procedures used by the TPA Manager for this check. 2. No specific sample size or selection methodology is defined for the review.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain a sample of receivable entries from the ERP system for the review period. 2. Obtain corresponding supporting documents (IPE-11) such as bank statements, collection reports, and invoices. 3. Obtain evidence of the TPA Manager's monthly review.
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that the receivable entries are recorded in the correct accounting period based on the supporting documents. 2. Verify that the TPA Manager's review was performed and documented.

subProcess: Customer Billing, Collection through RTGS, Collection through Cheque/Demand Draft
riskDescription: Risk of delay in recording the receipt of amounts from customers, leading to inaccurate cash and receivable balances.
controlObjective: To ensure timely and accurate recording of customer receipts in the ERP system.
controlActivity: The TPA Manager (WHO) randomly checks (WHAT) for the timely recording of receivables (WHY) in the ERP system (WHERE) on a monthly basis (WHEN) by comparing receipt dates with ERP entry dates (HOW).
controlEvidence: ERP system reports, bank statements, TPA Manager's review sign-off/report
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not define the specific methodology for 'random check' (e.g., sample size, selection criteria). 2. No documentation requirements for the random check are specified.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain a sample of cash receipts from bank statements or collection reports for the review period. 2. Obtain corresponding receivable entries from the ERP system. 3. Obtain evidence of the TPA Manager's monthly random check.
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that the receipt amounts are recorded in the ERP system in a timely manner, comparing the date of receipt with the date of ERP entry. 2. Verify that the TPA Manager's random check was performed and documented.

riskDescription: Risk that the daily bank statement verification activity is not performed regularly by the TPA Executive, leading to unrecorded or delayed recording of collections.
controlObjective: To ensure the TPA Executive consistently performs daily bank statement verification for collections.
controlActivity: The Manager - Accounts or Internal Auditor (WHO) randomly checks (WHAT) the adherence of the daily bank statement verification activity performed by the TPA Executive (WHY) on a monthly basis (WHEN) by reviewing a sample of daily bank statements and TPA Executive's confirmations (HOW).
controlEvidence: Daily bank statements, TPA Executive's confirmation emails/reports, Manager - Accounts/Internal Auditor's review documentation
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not define the specific methodology for 'random check' (e.g., sample size, selection criteria). 2. No specific documentation or report is mentioned for the TPA Executive's daily verification and confirmation.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain a sample of daily bank statements for the review period. 2. Obtain corresponding confirmation records from the TPA Executive to AM - Bid & Auctions. 3. Obtain evidence of the Manager - Accounts/Internal Auditor's monthly review.
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that the TPA Executive performed daily bank statement verification and provided confirmation as per the process. 2. Verify that the Manager - Accounts/Internal Auditor's random check was performed and documented.

riskDescription: Risk of delay in intimating AM – Bid & Auctions about missing customer details, leading to delays in collection and potential understatement of revenue.
controlObjective: To ensure timely communication of missing customer details to facilitate collections.
controlActivity: The TPA Manager (WHO) checks (WHAT) that required details (IPE-11) are communicated on an immediate basis to AM – Bid & Auctions (WHY) whenever information is missing from the bank statement (WHEN) by reviewing communication records (HOW).
controlEvidence: Communication records (emails), TPA Manager's review documentation
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not specify how the TPA Manager performs this check (e.g., specific report, sample review). 2. No system-generated alerts or reports are mentioned to highlight delayed intimations.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain a sample of instances where bank statements lacked required customer information. 2. Obtain communication records (e.g., emails) from TPA Executive to AM - Bid & Auctions for these instances. 3. Obtain evidence of the TPA Manager's review.
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that the TPA Executive communicated the missing details to AM - Bid & Auctions immediately (within the same day as per RT3). 2. Verify that the TPA Manager's check was performed.

riskDescription: Risk of incorrect or incomplete customer information being received, leading to errors in recording entries in ERP and incorrect customer balances.
controlObjective: To ensure accurate and complete customer information is obtained for ERP entries.
controlActivity: The AM – Bid & Auctions (WHO) cross-checks (WHAT) all the relevant information (IPE-11) required for recording entries in ERP (WHY) when collecting details from customers (WHEN) by verifying against internal requirements or a checklist (HOW).
controlEvidence: Customer information records (IPE-11), internal checklists/guidelines, AM - Bid & Auctions' review documentation
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not define a specific checklist or standard for the 'relevant information' (IPE-11). 2. No system-enforced validation is mentioned to ensure completeness and correctness of information before sharing with TPA Executive.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain a sample of customer information (IPE-11) collected by AM - Bid & Auctions. 2. Obtain internal guidelines or a checklist for required information. 3. Obtain evidence of AM - Bid & Auctions' cross-check.
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that all required information (IPE-11) was obtained and is accurate based on internal guidelines. 2. Verify that AM - Bid & Auctions performed the cross-check.

subProcess: Collection through RTGS, Collection through Cheque/Demand Draft
riskDescription: Risk that invoice-wise knocking-off of payments is not performed, leading to incorrect customer balances and potential overstatement of receivables.
controlObjective: To ensure timely identification and follow-up on outstanding customer payments to maintain accurate customer balances.
controlActivity: The TPA Manager (WHO) extracts a pending invoice report (IPE-14) (WHAT) on a monthly basis (WHEN) from the ERP system (WHERE) to identify long pending invoices with outstanding payments (WHY), and shares it with AM – Bid & Auctions for follow-up with the customer (HOW).
controlEvidence: Pending invoice reports (IPE-14), email communications, follow-up records
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not define a specific threshold for what constitutes 'long pending' invoices. 2. No clear process or documentation is specified for AM - Bid & Auctions' follow-up actions.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain monthly pending invoice reports (IPE-14) extracted by the TPA Manager. 2. Obtain evidence of these reports being shared with AM - Bid & Auctions. 3. Obtain a sample of long pending invoices and verify follow-up actions by AM - Bid & Auctions.
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that the TPA Manager extracts and shares the pending invoice report monthly. 2. Verify that follow-up actions are initiated by AM - Bid & Auctions for identified long pending invoices.
remarks: This control applies to both RTGS and Cheque/DD collection processes.

subProcess: Collection through RTGS, Collection through Cheque/Demand Draft
riskDescription: Risk that incorrect terms as per the Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) are considered during the verification of invoices and amounts received, leading to incorrect short receipt calculations.
controlObjective: To ensure accurate calculation of short receipts based on PPA terms.
controlActivity: The TPA Manager (WHO) cross-checks (WHAT) that the terms considered in the invoice are in line with the terms of the PPA (WHY) when a short receipt of amount is identified (WHEN) by comparing the invoice details with the PPA document (HOW).
controlEvidence: Invoices, PPA documents, TPA Manager's review documentation
gapsIdentified: 1. No specific checklist or system integration is mentioned to automatically compare invoice terms with PPA terms. 2. The manual comparison is prone to human error.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain a sample of invoices with short receipts. 2. Obtain the corresponding PPA documents. 3. Obtain evidence of the TPA Manager's cross-check.
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that the terms considered in the invoice align with the PPA terms. 2. Verify that the TPA Manager performed the cross-check and documented any discrepancies.
remarks: This control applies to both RTGS and Cheque/DD collection processes.

subProcess: Collection through RTGS, Collection through Cheque/Demand Draft
riskDescription: Risk of delay in intimating AM - Bid & Auctions and Manager - Accounts about partial receipt of amount, leading to delayed follow-up and potential understatement of revenue.
controlObjective: To ensure timely communication of partial receipt details for prompt follow-up.
controlActivity: The TPA Manager (WHO) checks (WHAT) that correct details about partial receipt of amount are communicated within 1 day of receipt of partial amount (WHY) to AM - Bid & Auctions and Manager - Accounts (WHERE) by reviewing communication records (HOW).
controlEvidence: Communication records (emails), TPA Manager's review documentation
gapsIdentified: 1. No system-generated alerts or reports are mentioned to highlight delayed intimations. 2. The manual review might miss instances of delayed communication.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain a sample of instances with partial receipt of amounts. 2. Obtain communication records (e.g., emails) from TPA Executive to AM - Bid & Auctions and Manager - Accounts for these instances. 3. Obtain evidence of the TPA Manager's review.
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that the TPA Executive communicated the partial receipt details to AM - Bid & Auctions and Manager - Accounts within 1 day of receipt. 2. Verify that the TPA Manager's check was performed.
remarks: This control applies to both RTGS and Cheque/DD collection processes.

subProcess: Collection through RTGS, Collection through Cheque/Demand Draft
riskDescription: Risk that reasons for short receipt of amount are not available or inaccurate, leading to unresolved discrepancies and incorrect customer balances.
controlObjective: To ensure valid and accurate reasons are documented for all short receipts.
controlActivity: The Manager - Accounts (WHO) checks (WHAT) for the accuracy of the reasons (IPE-12) provided by AM – Bid & Auctions and ensures proper basis is present for partial receipt of amount (WHY) when AM - Bid & Auctions confirms reasons for short receipt (WHEN) by reviewing supporting documentation (HOW).
controlEvidence: Reasons for short receipt (IPE-12), supporting documents, Manager - Accounts' review sign-off
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not define specific criteria or documentation standards for 'proper basis' for partial receipt. 2. The manual review is reliant on the Manager - Accounts' judgment.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain a sample of short receipts with reasons (IPE-12) provided by AM - Bid & Auctions. 2. Obtain supporting documentation for the reasons. 3. Obtain evidence of the Manager - Accounts' review.
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify the accuracy of the reasons (IPE-12) provided by AM - Bid & Auctions. 2. Verify that proper basis/documentation is present for the partial receipt. 3. Verify that the Manager - Accounts' check was performed.
remarks: This control applies to both RTGS and Cheque/DD collection processes.

subProcess: Collection through RTGS, Collection through Cheque/Demand Draft
riskDescription: Risk of incorrect computation of interest (IPE-15) to be charged to the customer for late payments, leading to revenue misstatement or customer disputes.
controlObjective: To ensure accurate calculation and charging of interest for late customer payments.
controlActivity: The Manager - Accounts (WHO) checks (WHAT) that the interest amount (IPE-15) calculated by the TPA Executive is in line with the applicable terms of the PPA (WHY) when interest is to be charged for late receipt (WHEN) by comparing the calculation with PPA terms (HOW).
controlEvidence: Interest calculation sheet (IPE-15), PPA documents, Manager - Accounts' review sign-off
gapsIdentified: 1. No system-automated calculation or validation of interest based on PPA terms is mentioned. 2. The manual calculation and review are prone to human error.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain a sample of late receipts where interest was charged. 2. Obtain the TPA Executive's interest calculation sheet (IPE-15) and the relevant PPA terms. 3. Obtain evidence of the Manager - Accounts' review.
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that the interest amount (IPE-15) is calculated correctly as per the PPA terms. 2. Verify that the Manager - Accounts performed the check and documented any discrepancies.
remarks: This control applies to both RTGS and Cheque/DD collection processes.

subProcess: Collection through RTGS, Collection through Cheque/Demand Draft
riskDescription: Risk of unauthorized entries being posted in the ERP system (IPE-10), leading to fraudulent transactions or financial misstatement.
controlObjective: To ensure that only authorized personnel can post entries in the ERP system.
controlActivity: Access rights (WHAT) to record entries in the ERP system (IPE-10) (WHERE) are restricted to authorized personnel only (WHO) at all times (WHEN) to prevent unauthorized transactions (WHY) through system configuration (HOW).
controlEvidence: ERP access matrix, user access logs, access review reports
segregationOfDuties: Separate roles for transaction initiation, approval, and posting.
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP does not detail the process for defining and reviewing authorized personnel. 2. No mention of periodic review of access rights to ensure they remain appropriate and are revoked upon role changes or termination.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain the ERP access matrix and list of authorized personnel for posting entries (IPE-10). 2. Obtain evidence of periodic access reviews. 3. Obtain a sample of ERP entries and verify the user who posted them.
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that only authorized personnel have access to record entries in the ERP system. 2. Verify that access rights are reviewed periodically. 3. Verify that actual entries are posted by authorized users.
remediationActionPlan: Implement a formal process for periodic review of ERP access rights, including segregation of duties analysis.
remarks: This control applies to both RTGS and Cheque/DD collection processes.

subProcess: Collection through RTGS, Collection through Cheque/Demand Draft
riskDescription: Risk of duplicate recording of amounts received, leading to overstatement of cash and understatement of receivables.
controlObjective: To prevent duplicate recording of customer receipts in the ERP system.
controlActivity: Controls (WHAT) are built in the ERP system (WHERE) to automatically provide a warning or restrict the recording of duplicate amounts with the same document reference number (WHY) at the time of entry (WHEN) through system configuration (HOW).
controlEvidence: ERP configuration settings, system test results, error logs
gapsIdentified: 1. The SOP states 'Controls in ERP to be built' which implies it might be a recommendation or not fully implemented. 2. No details on the specific configuration or how the warning/restriction functions are provided.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain ERP configuration documents related to duplicate entry checks. 2. Perform a system walkthrough to verify the functionality of duplicate amount warnings/restrictions. 3. Obtain a sample of attempted duplicate entries (if available) to confirm the control's operation.
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that the ERP system is configured to prevent or warn against duplicate entries with the same document reference number. 2. Confirm that the control effectively prevents or flags duplicate recordings.
remediationActionPlan: Confirm the implementation and effectiveness of the ERP duplicate entry controls.
remarks: This control applies to both RTGS and Cheque/DD collection processes.

subProcess: Collection through RTGS, Collection through Cheque/Demand Draft
riskDescription: Risk that entries are posted to incorrect General Ledger (GL) accounts or with incorrect amounts/customer accounts in ERP, leading to financial misstatement.
controlObjective: To ensure accurate GL coding, amounts, and customer accounts for all receivable entries.
controlActivity: The TPA Manager (WHO) checks (WHAT) that all receivables are coded to the correct GL and are posted with the correct amount and in the correct customer account (WHY) in the ERP system (IPE-10) (WHERE) on a per transaction basis (WHEN) by reviewing supporting documents and ERP entries (HOW).
controlEvidence: ERP entries (IPE-10), supporting documents, TPA Manager's review sign-off
gapsIdentified: 1. No specific report or reconciliation process is mentioned for this check. 2. Manual review of every entry might be inefficient or prone to error for high transaction volumes.
todDataValidated: 1. Obtain a sample of recorded receivable entries (IPE-10) from the ERP system. 2. Obtain corresponding supporting documents (e.g., invoices, bank statements). 3. Obtain evidence of the TPA Manager's review.
todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that the GL coding, amount, and customer account in the ERP entry match the supporting documentation. 2. Verify that the TPA Manager's check was performed and documented.
remarks: This control addresses risks R31 (Entry posted in incorrect GL) and R32 (Entry posted with incorrect amount). It applies to both RTGS and Cheque/DD collection processes.

subProcess: Collection through RTGS, Collection through Cheque/Demand Draft
riskDescription: Risk that approval for raising debit notes is not obtained as per the Delegation of Authority (DoA) matrix, leading to unauthorized financial transactions.
controlObjective: To ensure all debit notes are approved according to the Delegation of Authority.
controlActivity: The TPA Executive (WHO) checks (WHAT) that approval for raising a debit note is as per DoA (WHY) before posting the entry in the ERP system (IPE-10) (WHERE) on a per transaction basis (WHEN) by reviewing the approval documentation against the DoA matrix (HOW).

riskDescription: Risk that Cheque/DD clearance status is not monitored on a daily basis, leading to delays in identifying bounced cheques or uncollected funds.

riskDescription: Risk that knocking-off of payments received against invoices/invoice based knocking-off procedure not performed leading to possibility of incorrect customer balances.

todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that the TPA Manager performed the cross-check for the selected cases. 2. Confirm that the terms considered in the invoice align with the PPA terms. 3. Verify that the reasons for short receipt are adequately supported.

todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that Manager - Accounts reviewed the accuracy of reasons provided by AM - Bid & Auctions. 2. Confirm that proper basis/documentation exists for the partial receipt. 3. Assess if the reasons are consistent with company policy or PPA terms.

riskDescription: Risk of incorrect computation of interest (IPE-15) to be charged to the customer for late receipt, leading to inaccurate revenue recognition or customer disputes.

todChecksPerformed: 1. Verify that the Manager - Accounts checked the interest calculation. 2. Recalculate the interest amount based on PPA terms and verify against IPE-15. 3. Confirm that the calculated interest is in line with PPA terms.
